estimates.anchor_source: No tradable market (Polymarket public-search and Kalshi KXABNB fetched 2026-09-17T03:41:48Z: price ladders and Q3 bookings only). Designated anchor: the team's market-implied model input (research/notes/2026-09-13_market-implied-model.md) that $1,050M/q 'exhausts the $3.4bn authorisation by 2Q27, so a new programme is the likely 4Q26 or 1Q27 announcement', read as P(announce by Feb) 0.65 x P(size >= $5bn | announce) 0.78 = 0.51. A repo note, not a market; flagged NOT_INDEPENDENTLY_DERIVED on provenance.

model.structure: pace ~ N(1.06, 0.13) USD bn/q for 3Q26 and 4Q26 -> remaining at 5 Nov (~$2.3bn) and at Feb (~$1.28bn, 1.25 quarters of pace); logistic trigger f(r)=1/(1+exp(2.0(r-1.45))) fitted to the 16-print state panel (announced at 0, 1.0-1.2, 1.5-1.6 quarters remaining; never at >=2.7) -> P(announce 5 Nov) 0.19, P(announce Feb | not Nov) 0.57; size >= $5bn 0.78 (last two programs $6bn = 1.3-1.6x FCF; FY26 FCF $4.4-4.8bn); leg B hazard 0.06 (0.14 after a November authorization); union 0.544, +0.01 judgement.

impact.note: Immaterial. A renewal of the $6bn program at the existing pace is the base case and is already in the FY27 share count (595.8m -> 573.0m); authorizations are announced only inside the letter and the event study cannot distinguish their abnormal return from zero (09_stock-behaviour-and-alpha.md s6). The memo's 'floor on sell-offs, not a catalyst' line stands. A pace step-change (>= $1.5bn in Q4, P ~0.08) would be a +$2.5 signal; the record shows no opportunistic step-up after sell-offs (3Q25 $877M after -8.0%; 1Q26 $1,088M after -6.2%).
